transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Hi. Thanks for seeing me. Um, basically, what brings me in is that I'm losing hours of my day just... rechecking things. It's getting really hard to manage. 

I'll get stuck checking my dressing supplies, the door locks at home, or stuff for work—I'm an engineer, so things like file dimensions and my revision notes. And it’s not just a quick glance to make sure it's right. I don't feel allowed to move on to the next task until I've gone through the exact same checking routine enough times. I basically just have to keep doing it over and over until the anxiety finally drops.
When you feel you have to recheck, do unwanted thoughts or images pop into your mind that something bad will happen if you don’t?

Yeah, that's exactly it. It's like... even after I know I’ve cleaned the wound area, or I've already reviewed a CAD file for work, this thought just keeps cutting in. It tells me that I missed one tiny thing, and because of that, it’s going to turn into a bad infection, or... or a design mistake that ends up actually hurting someone. I try to tell myself it's fine, but I just can’t reason it away. The thought just stays there until I check again.
When the thought hits that you might have missed something, do you then feel driven to repeat a specific checking ritual?

Yeah, exactly. Like I was saying before, that's what ends up costing me hours of my day. Once that thought hits, I feel like I'm just not allowed to move on to whatever I need to do next. I have to go back and do the exact same checking routine—whether it's the dressing supplies, the door locks, or those file dimensions at work—over and over again. I just keep repeating the steps until the anxiety finally drops enough for me to stop.
Do you recognize that these repeated checking thoughts and routines are excessive or unreasonable, even while they’re happening?

Um... I'm not really sure. I guess I haven't really noticed or thought about it like that. In the moment, the fear feels so real that the checking doesn't seem unreasonable to me at all—it just feels like something I absolutely have to do. I just know the anxiety is there and I have to do the routine to fix it, so I don't really stop to think if it's excessive right then.
When you're not actively checking, do these thoughts about having missed something still pop into your mind against your will?

Yeah, they really do. Like I was saying earlier... even when I'm away from it, like after I already know I’ve cleaned that wound area, or I'm completely done reviewing a CAD file for the day. I'll be doing something else, and the thought just cuts right back in. 

It just pops up totally against my will, telling me I missed one tiny thing and now it’s going to turn into a bad infection, or a design mistake that ends up hurting someone. I really don't want the thought there, and I try to tell myself I already checked, but I can’t just reason it away. It just invades my head.
Right now, do you believe the fear is actually true that if you don’t check enough, someone will probably be harmed?

Um... I'm not really sure. I guess I don't know how to answer that. Right now, sitting here, I don't know if I actually believe it's definitely true that someone will get hurt. It's hard to say. I just don't really know.
Sitting here right now, is it possible that these fears are not actually true?

I mean, I suppose it's possible. Like I said, I'm just really not sure. It's hard to separate the feeling of it from what's actually real, so... I guess it could be false, but I just don't know for certain.
Do these thoughts feel like your own thoughts, even though they’re unwanted?

Yeah, they do. I mean, I know they're coming from my own head. It's not like I'm hearing voices or someone else is putting them there. They're my thoughts, it's just... I don't want to be thinking them. But yeah, I know they're mine.
Right now, do you think your fear that someone will be harmed if you don’t keep checking is probably true?

I mean... it's kind of like what I was saying a minute ago. I just really don't know for sure. Logically, sitting here talking to you, I guess I wouldn't say it's *probably* true. But the feeling is just so strong that I can't completely rule it out either. It's just a really intense "what if" that I can't shake, even if part of me knows the odds of it actually happening don't make sense.
Even when you’re not anxious about harm or checking, do you generally feel a strong need for things to be done in a very exact, perfect way?

Not really, no. I mean, I'm an engineer, so obviously I have to pay attention to detail at work, but in my day-to-day life... no, I wouldn't say I need things to be perfect. 

My apartment isn't super neat or anything, and I don't really care if things on my desk are lined up a certain way or if a task is done exactly right. It's really just the checking. When I'm not having those specific worries about someone getting hurt, I'm actually pretty laid back about how things are done. I don't really have that perfectionist drive you're talking about.
When the thought that you missed something pops into your mind, does it feel like a thought your own mind is producing?

Yeah, um... like I was saying a little bit ago, it definitely does. It's just my own brain coming up with the idea that I missed something. I know it's me thinking it, it's not like an outside voice or anything like that. It's just my own mind doing it, even if I don't want it to.
When the fear comes up that you missed something and someone could be harmed, do you usually think that fear is probably true?

I think it's pretty much what I was just saying a minute ago. Um... even in the moment when the fear is really hitting me, I don't know if I actually believe it's *probably* true. 

My logical brain still kind of knows the odds are really low. It's just that the doubt gets so loud, and I feel like I can't be one hundred percent sure it's false. So I end up feeling like I have to check anyway, just in case. But no, even when the anxiety is bad, I wouldn't say I think the fear is highly likely to happen. I'm just stuck on the "what if."
Do you ever find yourself checking repeatedly even when no intrusive thought about harm has come into your mind first?

No, I don't think so. The checking is pretty much always tied to those specific thoughts. If I don't have that worry pop up about missing something or someone getting hurt, I don't feel any urge to go back and look at things. It's really just a reaction to the thought happening first.
